title: Choose an appropriate chart
description: Match the chart to comparison, distribution, relationship or change over time.
accomplishes: Match the chart to comparison, distribution, relationship or change over time. Specify axes, units, labels and uncertainty treatment. Explain misleading alternatives and distinguish missing observations from zero. Do not fabricate data to make a chart attractive.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst.

Task: Choose an appropriate chart.

Input context:
- QUESTION: [QUESTION]
- FIELDS: [FIELDS]
- AUDIENCE: [AUDIENCE]
- DATA LIMITS: [DATA LIMITS]

Match the chart to comparison, distribution, relationship or change over time. Specify axes, units, labels and uncertainty treatment. Explain misleading alternatives and distinguish missing observations from zero. Do not fabricate data to make a chart attractive.

Use authorised, anonymised or fictional data. Never fabricate statistical significance, causal findings or executed analysis.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Monthly enquiry chart
Use a labelled time series for comparable monthly totals and mark any incomplete period. A bar comparison may be clearer for a few service categories. Avoid a pie chart when categories overlap. Include definitions and source dates. Chart choice improves interpretation, but it cannot repair inconsistent tracking or establish a business explanation by itself.
